name: HAZUS highway bridges
source: FEMA, Hazus Earthquake Model Technical Manual, Hazus 6.1, July 2024, Section 7.1 (Tables 7-1, 7-2 and 7-6; Equations 7-1 to 7-4)
implemented_by: E. Taciroglu, in tools/hazus_bridges.py of ShakeReady. The classes and median values themselves are FEMA's, from the manual named in "source".
intensity_measure_also_needed: SA(0.3) for the Kshape factor, classes with ishape = 1

adjustments.k_3d: 1 + A / (N - B), N = number of spans
adjustments.slight: median * min(1, k_shape) if ishape = 1, else median

transcription: Tables 7-1, 7-2 and 7-6 were transcribed from the manual and compared by script against the text extracted from the manual's PDF: all 28 sets of medians, and the K3D equation, I-shape value and design era of the 27 classes that have them.
verification: The code reproduces the worked example in Section 7.1.6.2 of the manual (class HWB17, K3D = 1.125; damage-state probabilities 0.183, 0.205, 0.165, 0.255, 0.192 against the manual's rounded 0.18, 0.20, 0.16, 0.26, 0.20). The classification passes against every row of Table 7-1.

decisions.choice: A California bridge built in 1975 or later is classed as seismic design; elsewhere the year is 1990.
decisions.basis: Table 7-1 gives the year in every row. The sentence introducing the table states the two years the other way round (1990 in California, 1975 elsewhere). The table is followed because it is explicit row by row and agrees with earlier editions of the Hazus documentation.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.topic: Form of the span factor K3D
decisions.choice: K3D = 1 + A / (N - B), with A and B from Table 7-2 and N the number of spans.
decisions.basis: Table 7-2 and the accompanying text give this form. Equation 7-3 is printed as (1 + A) / (N - B), but the manual's worked example evaluates it to 1.125 for A = 0.25, B = 1 and N = 3, which only the Table 7-2 form gives.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: K3D is taken as 1 when N - B is zero or negative.
decisions.basis: The formula is undefined in that case and the manual does not say what to do. A factor of 1 leaves the class medians unchanged.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: K3D is taken as 1 and the spectral-shape factor is not applied. The skew factor still applies.
decisions.basis: Table 7-1 gives no K3D equation and no I-shape value for HWB28.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: N is NBI Item 45, the number of spans in the main unit. Approach spans (Item 46) are not counted.
decisions.basis: The manual's worked example takes the number of spans from Item 45.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: 'Length less than 20 m' is evaluated on NBI Item 49, the structure length.
decisions.basis: Table 7-1 does not name the NBI item. Step 1 of the damage algorithm lists bridge length separately from maximum span length, so the total length is used.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: A skew coded 99 is evaluated as 45 degrees. Any other value of 90 or more is evaluated as 0.
decisions.basis: The NBI uses 99 when skew varies along the bridge, and the manual does not address this code. 45 degrees is unfavorable but bounded. A published implementation for Texas bridges treats the same code with its 45-degree adjustment (Khosravikia et al., 2020, CTR Technical Report 5-6916-01-1).
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: Only damage from ground shaking is evaluated.
decisions.basis: The manual's ground-failure functions need permanent ground deformation at each site, and no such hazard layer is available here.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: Culverts are kept in the inventory and classified by the same rules as bridges.
decisions.basis: The NBI records culverts as structures and Table 7-1 has no separate rule for them. Bridge curves fit culverts poorly, and users may wish to exclude them.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.choice: The design era is taken from the year built alone.
decisions.basis: The NBI has no field for seismic retrofit. The year of reconstruction is not used, because a reconstruction is not necessarily a seismic one. Bridges retrofitted after construction are therefore treated as unretrofitted.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.

decisions.topic: Slight-damage median shown on the map
decisions.choice: Bridge popups show the class value for slight damage, without the spectral-shape factor.
decisions.basis: The factor needs Sa(0.3 s) and Sa(1.0 s) at the site, which come from a hazard layer. It is applied when damage is computed.
decisions.status: In use. Recorded at the request of the project lead; open to review.
